chunks: And indeed, among the matters concerning the owner of the donkey, whose story was revealed in the Quran, the People of the Book claim that he was a prophet; so God Almighty caused him to die for a hundred years, then raised him, and his food and drink remained unchanged.

And that was an extraordinary event. And similar to what we have mentioned are many things narrated by the authors of biographies and histories regarding the kings of Persia, their concealment from their companions for a period during which their whereabouts were unknown, then their return and appearance for a certain purpose, and although the Quran did not explicitly mention this, it is recorded in the histories.

And likewise, a group of the sages of Rome and India had periods of concealment and states of being that were outside the norm; we do not mention them because the opponent may deny them, following their habit of denying reports, and they are recorded in the histories.

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْحِمَارِ: The owner of the donkey (Quranic figure)

ai.seo_question: What historical and Quranic precedents are cited for the occultation of the Imam?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi leverages the Quranic narrative of the man of the donkey (2:259) alongside historical accounts of Persian kings and sages to establish the plausibility of the Imam's occultation as a known divine phenomenon rather than an unprecedented miracle. By citing these precedents from both scripture and secular histories, he counters skeptics who might deny such events, framing the Imam's concealment within a broader tradition of divine preservation and hiddenness.
